issues.body: axis_exceeds compares spent + charge against total + total * BUDGET_REL_TOL. For every positive total, this deliberately accepts representable cumulative spend strictly greater than total when the excess falls within the relative 1e-12 allowance. That contradicts the documented rule that a charge exceeding either total is refused fail-closed and invalidates the claimed exact basic-composition cap. The small-delta tests exercise a zero total and a charge exactly equal to a tiny total; neither exercises a representable just-over-budget cumulative value inside the allowed tolerance.
issues.fix_hint: Remove positive acceptance slack from the configured totals. Use conservative accounting that cannot authorize cumulative epsilon or delta above the configured total, such as exact/fixed-point accounting after validated conversion or deliberately conservative rounding. Add a regression test constructing a representable spent + charge just above a positive total by less than total * 1e-12, and assert that charge is refused without mutating either spent axis.
issues.title: Relative tolerance still authorizes privacy-budget overspend

verdict.summary: Round 6 is stagnant. The prior major finding remains unchanged: axis_exceeds permits spent + charge to exceed the configured total by total * 1e-12, despite the public fail-closed and basic sequential-composition claims. The tests still cover zero delta and an exact tiny-total boundary, but not a representable cumulative charge just above a positive total within the accepted relative slack. Because delta is a cryptographic failure-probability axis, deliberately authorizing any positive excess contradicts the documented accounting bound.
